title: bug: doctor's worktree control-branch and target probes check only refs/heads, so doctor exits 0 on two states that stop the fleet: a target branch origin does not have (remote mode cuts every new task worktree from refs/remotes/origin/<target>, so each worker seat dies at its first claim with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED) and a moe/control that diverged from the target (the control checkout stops following with MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED and QA's landed gate stops every QA claim)
description:
Filed by defect hunt task-3488566e (11-04 #17, lane 3: doctor's probes against worktree mode as it runs now). HEAD bb0bc17e.

PROBLEM
- packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctorWorktree.ts:102-112 (probeTarget) only asks whether refs/heads/<target> resolves and whether a worktree has it checked out. The launchers need more than that:
  - Both launchers are in remote mode whenever `git remote` prints anything (no_git_remote, scripts/moe-agent.sh:6062-6065). There they cut each new task worktree from refs/remotes/origin/<target>. When that ref is missing after the fetch, they stop the seat: moe-agent.sh:3450-3455 and moe-agent.ps1:3432-3436 raise MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, and worktree_stop (moe-agent.sh:3227-3235) report_blocks the claimed task and exits 1. That happens once per worker claim.
  - A local target holding commits origin lacks also fails every landing with MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED (moe-agent.sh:7390).
- doctorWorktree.ts:94-100 (probeControlBranch) only compares `symbolic-ref HEAD` with refs/heads/moe/control.
  - The control follow needs moe/control to be an ancestor of the target. Otherwise moe-agent.sh:7019-7021 raises MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED ("nothing was reset, reconcile it by hand").
  - QA's landed gate (moe-agent.sh:7083-7084) then stops with MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND for every completion landed after the divergence. Until task-3416b309 lands, each such stop exits the QA wrapper.
  - Agent commits there are refused by c4cd6dce's guard, but a human commit from the IDE's commit dialog is not: the control checkout is the IDE project.
- The docs make doctor the gate: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:1254-1255 (the control branch and target rows, which state only today's checks) and :1289 ("Run doctor; it must exit 0. Then relaunch the seats").

EVIDENCE: architect re-run at bb0bc17e, /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-3488566e/mine/doctor-worktree-refs-rerun.txt (subagent originals in B/remote-target-missing.txt and B/control-diverged.txt).
- Fresh fixture: a bare origin holding only main, a local moe/work-2026-10-24, HEAD moe/control, worktreeMode on.
  [OK] worktree control branch: control checkout is on refs/heads/moe/control
  [OK] worktree target: target moe/work-2026-10-24 exists and is not checked out in any worktree
  The launcher's check: fatal: couldn't find remote ref moe/work-2026-10-24; rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/moe/work-2026-10-24 rc=1 (=> MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED).
- Diverged fixture: a commit on moe/control that the target lacks, plus a landing on the target.
  merge-base --is-ancestor moe/control target rc=1 (=> MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED)
  [OK] worktree control branch ... / [OK] worktree target ... / doctor exit=0
- Live today, refs/remotes/origin/moe/work-2026-10-24, the local target and moe/control are all bb0bc17e, so the fix raises no false FAIL here.

FIX DIRECTION. Offline reads only: doctor still never fetches.
- probeTarget: when `git remote` lists any remote (the launchers' rule), also require refs/remotes/origin/<target> to resolve to a commit. Require refs/heads/<target> to be its ancestor: `merge-base --is-ancestor`, where exit 1 is a FAIL naming MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED.
- probeControlBranch: when HEAD is moe/control, run `merge-base --is-ancestor refs/heads/moe/control refs/heads/<target>`:
  - exit 0 passes, because behind or equal is normal between a landing and the follow;
  - exit 1 fails, naming MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED;
  - any other exit fails as unreadable.
- Update the two TROUBLESHOOTING.md rows to state these conditions.
- Out of scope: the launchers (held by open rows), doctor.ts's daemon.json probe, docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctorWorktree.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.test.ts (the "worktree readiness probes" and "worktree probes against a real repository" describes), docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md (worktree-mode readiness table, rows :1254-1255 only). No open row holds any of them (lanes.js 06:50Z).
definitionOfDone: doctor.test.ts stub-git cases. With `git remote` answering "origin" and refs/remotes/origin/<target> unresolvable, the result is a `[FAIL] worktree target:` line naming that ref, exit 1. With that ref resolving but `merge-base --is-ancestor refs/heads/<target> refs/remotes/origin/<target>` exiting 1, the result is a `[FAIL] worktree target:` line naming MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED, exit 1. A repo whose `git remote` prints nothing keeps today's [OK] line, and the existing 'runs only bounded read-only Git commands, never the quality gate' case still passes, with no fetch.

doctor.test.ts real-repository cases. When moe/control holds a commit the target lacks, the result is `[FAIL] worktree control branch:` naming MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED, exit 1. When the target is ahead of moe/control (moe/control is its ancestor), the result is `[OK] worktree control branch`, exit 0.

docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md's control-branch and target rows state the ancestry and origin conditions (grep 'ancestor' and 'refs/remotes/origin' hit them), and `npx vitest run src/commands/doctor.test.ts src/commands/doctor.bindHost.test.ts` passes in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.description:
Control ancestry, in packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctorWorktree.ts. The prototype is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-3950184e/doctorWorktree.ts.

(1) The `Git` type's failure branch gains `code?: number`, with a one-line comment that it is git's numeric exit status.
- In probeWorktreeReadiness's git wrapper catch, keep why: describeGitFailure(err).
- Add code only when (err as { code?: unknown } | null)?.code is a number. That is execFile's exit status; ENOENT and the maxBuffer code are strings and stay out.

(2) Add isAncestor(git, ancestor, descendant): Promise<boolean | string>. It runs ['merge-base', '--is-ancestor', ancestor, descendant]:
- ok gives true;
- code 1 gives false;
- any other failure gives its why.

(3) probeControlBranch:
- When HEAD is not CONTROL_REF, keep today's message.
- When HEAD is CONTROL_REF and cachedPlanRef(target) is undefined, keep today's pass 'control checkout is on refs/heads/moe/control'. The target line already fails a non-literal name.
- Otherwise, follows = isAncestor(CONTROL_REF, `refs/heads/${target}`):
  - true: pass 'control checkout is on refs/heads/moe/control, an ancestor of <target>';
  - false: fail '<CONTROL_REF> holds commits <target> lacks, so the control checkout cannot follow the target (MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED) and QA's landed gate stops every claim; reconcile moe/control by hand';
  - a why: fail 'cannot tell whether <CONTROL_REF> is an ancestor of <target> (<why>)'.
- Behind or equal passes. Between a landing and the follow, moe/control is legitimately behind, and moe-agent.sh:7019-7021 refuses only exit 1.

Error handling: every git failure becomes one bounded line through verdict(), [FAIL] while worktree mode is on and [INFO] while it is off. Nothing throws. Doctor stays read-only: runGit keeps --no-optional-locks and protocol.allow=never, and merge-base and remote write nothing.
implementationPlan.note: Control ancestry in doctorWorktree.ts: Git failure branch gains numeric code (execFile exit status only), new isAncestor() maps merge-base --is-ancestor exit 0/1/other to true/false/why, probeControlBranch fails MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED on exit 1 and as unreadable on any other failure, passes behind-or-equal. Edit tool only; read-only git reads, no fetch.

implementationPlan.description:
Remote mode for the target probe, in the same file (same prototype).

Keep probeTarget's literal-name, local rev-parse and checked-out checks. Bind `const origin = cachedPlanRef(target)`: it is the existing literal-branch-name rule AND returns refs/remotes/origin/<target>, so reuse it and hand-build nothing. When the checked-out check passes, return probeOriginTarget(git, target, ref, origin, hard).

probeOriginTarget:
1. git(['remote']).
   - A failure fails 'target <t>: cannot list remotes (<why>)'.
   - Empty output passes with today's message, 'target <t> exists and is not checked out in any worktree'. That is local mode, unchanged.
2. Any output is remote mode: the launchers' no_git_remote rule, moe-agent.sh:6062-6065.
   - `rev-parse --verify --quiet ${origin}^{commit}` failing fails 'target <t>: remote mode cuts every task worktree from <origin>, which does not resolve (<why>), so each worker seat would stop with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED; push <t> to origin, or fetch it'. This is moe-agent.sh:3450-3455.
3. Then contained = isAncestor(ref, origin):
   - true passes 'target <t> exists, is not checked out in any worktree, and <origin> contains it';
   - false fails 'target <t>: <ref> holds commits <origin> lacks, so every landing would stop with MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED; push or reconcile it (fetch first if origin moved elsewhere)'. This is sync_land_target, moe-agent.sh:7387-7391;
   - a why fails 'target <t>: cannot tell whether <ref> is an ancestor of <origin> (<why>)'.

Give probeOriginTarget a doc comment saying that remote mode is the launchers' any-remote rule, that they cut and land from origin's copy, and that doctor never fetches, so it reads that copy as last fetched.

Error handling: as in step 2. Every outcome is one verdict() line, and no git call can write.
